Rusted scaffolding and gantries cling to the rock face, draped with tangled cabling and pipework, hazard-striped and streaked with grime.
A bank of smelters glows molten orange behind grimy heat-shields, venting plumes of exhaust that drift and freeze in the vacuum.
Floodlight towers on hydraulic cranes blaze harsh white over the worksite, their beams thick with floating rock-dust and debris.
Ore conveyor belts grind steadily across the asteroid's surface, black rubber cracked and patched, carrying crushed rock toward the processing drums.
Bulging fuel tanks squat on reinforced brackets, their flanks stenciled with faded warning text and smeared with oil and chemical residue.
Battered haulers sit docked at the loading bay, hulls dented and scorched, umbilical hoses snaking into their bellies like industrial veins.
A crane swings a massive ore container through the dark, its chain trailing dust, hydraulic arm groaning under the dead weight.
Scarred drill-heads sit idle on the rig deck, their tungsten teeth chipped and blackened from hours boring into iron-rich rock.
Sparking welders crouch over a fractured support strut, their arc-light strobing blue-white through the grime and hanging mineral dust.
Stacked cargo containers line the staging platform, each one dented and repainted multiple times, identification codes barely legible beneath the rust.
Warning beacons pulse slow amber across the lower gantry level, their cracked lenses fogged with condensation and mineral deposit buildup.
Tangled pipework and cabling run along every wall and walkway, zip-tied and duct-taped at stress points, leaking faint vapor trails.
Yellow-black hazard stripes peel from blast doors and airlock frames, edges curling away to expose bare scoured metal underneath.
Exhaust plumes vent from processing stacks in rhythmic bursts, each cloud of superheated gas crystallizing instantly in the surrounding cold vacuum.
A mesh cage elevator rattles up the drill-tower exterior, its cable fraying visibly at the drum, loaded with muddy-booted workers.
Grime and oil streaks coat every horizontal surface, pooling in bolt-holes and weld seams, leaving dark fingerprints on every handle and rung.
An emergency pressure valve has been wired open with steel cable and hope, a handwritten tag warning crews not to touch it.
Loose tread-plate flooring rattles underfoot across the processing deck, held down by mismatched bolts, edges sharp where panels have buckled upward.
A idle rock-grinder sits chained down mid-platform, its intake hopper crusted with dried ore slurry, waiting on a replacement drive shaft.
Rows of atmosphere canisters are bolted to a bulkhead rack, some near-empty, their pressure gauges reading in faded hand-painted increments.
A portable generator unit chugs on a lower platform, exhaust blackening the rock above it, its casing held shut with banding strap.
Magnetic clamp rails run the length of the ore platform, their surfaces worn mirror-smooth by constant container traffic, bolts vibrating loose.
A busted floodlight hangs dark from its mount, replaced crudely by a cluster of work lamps zip-tied to the same strut.
Slurry drainage channels cut into the rock floor are clogged with mineral paste, overflowing black liquid across the lower equipment deck.
Safety netting sags between gantry levels, heavy with debris and loose bolting, its anchor points pulling slowly free of the rock wall.
